info.title: DAS Tag Manager API
info.description: DAS Tag Manager for one Network (containers and tags follow). Served on the Network host `<network>.tag-manager.<org domain>`. Conventions (docs/engineering/api-conventions.md): JSON in camelCase, instants in `*At` fields as ISO-8601 UTC, ids as prefixed ULIDs. Errors are RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` with a machine `code`. Authentication is an Organization session token bound to a Network; the Network a request acts for is ALWAYS the credential's, and the host must name it (403 `NETWORK_HOST_MISMATCH`). 401 and 403 problems apply to every authenticated operation; 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` when the Organisation API, which answers for the credential's Network, does not.

resources.name: policy_type
resources.description: A policy type of the credential's Network (the feature `policies`), with its platforms, target dimensions and configuration types, written by a Network admin. Its key never changes. `platforms` and `configuration_types` are lists replaced whole and answered sorted by key (write them in that order); `dimensions` is a set of target dimension keys (reference `das_tag_manager_policy_target_dimension.<name>.key` so the dimension is created first), and a dimension a live policy of the type targets cannot leave it; each configuration type's `fields` are field definitions in the field language of DAS Policies, one `jsonencode()` per field. Destroy archives it (`ARCHIVED`), refused while a policy or configuration of the type is not archived: a policy type is archived, never deleted.

destroy.reason: A policy type is archivable (P11): it is never deleted, so destroy archives it (refused while its policies or configurations are not archived).

resources.name: policy_target_dimension
resources.description: A target dimension of the credential's Network (the feature `policies`): what a policy's target names, with the definition of its values (`input`, the field language of DAS Policies) and its weight (1-10), written by a Network admin. Its key never changes. Which policy types may target it is each type's `dimensions`. Destroy deletes it (an archived policy type loses it), refused while a policy type that is not archived has it among its dimensions or a target names it.

resources.name: policy_site_platform
resources.description: A site-platform rule of the credential's Network (the feature `policies`): the sites whose code matches `pattern` (`*` for any characters) are on `platform`, the first matching rule by `position` winning. Written by a Network admin; a position is taken once in the Network.

resources.name: policy_catalogue
resources.description: A value catalogue of the credential's Network (the feature `policies`), written by an operator: the values fields of policy types and target dimensions offer as `catalogue.<key>`, and the sides of mappings. Its key never changes. `values` is the list of active values, kept in your order and replaced whole, each a plain text unique in the catalogue (archived values included) with an optional `label` and its `id`, which the API gives it: write a value's `id` (from the state after the first apply) to change its text and keep it, so the mappings' rows follow it; a value without `id` is the one with that text, or a new one. Any change of the catalogue, its label included, plans every `id` you did not write as known after apply. A value left out is archived: `archived_values` lists it, the mappings' rows keep it, and writing its text again restores it. Configurations, policies and defaults hold their own copies of values: a change here changes none of them. Destroy archives the catalogue (P11), refused while a policy type that is not archived reads it in a field, a target dimension reads it in its input or a mapping that is not archived has it as `from` or `to`; its key stays taken, so a new catalogue with it is 409: import the archived one and set `archived = false` to restore it.

destroy.reason: A catalogue is archivable (P11): it is never deleted, so destroy archives it (refused while a policy type, a target dimension or a mapping that is not archived reads it).

resources.name: policy_mapping
resources.description: A mapping between two value catalogues of the credential's Network (the feature `policies`), written by an operator: for each value of `from` (a row's `key`) the values of `to` it goes to (its `cells`), each value by its text (stored by the value's id, so a value whose text changes stays in the rows). Its key, `from`, `to` and `cell` never change, and a mapping is never deleted, so a change of one is an error at plan (reference `das_tag_manager_policy_catalogue.<name>.key` so the catalogues are created first). `cell` is the type of a cell's value in the field language of DAS Policies; without it a cell holds no value, with it each cell's `value_json` is one `jsonencode()` of its value. `rows` and their `cells` are lists kept in your order and replaced whole. A mapping is the template a `map` field of a configuration starts from: its rows change no configuration. Destroy archives it (P11), refused while a policy type that is not archived reads it in a field; its key stays taken, so a new mapping with it is 409: import the archived one and set `archived = false` to restore it. A mapping without a cell type is a new mapping too: removing `cell` from the Terraform configuration (`.tf`) never turns this mapping into one.

destroy.reason: A mapping is archivable (P11): it is never deleted, so destroy archives it (refused while a policy type that is not archived reads it).

resources.changeInstead: To change its key, from, to or cell, create a new mapping with a new key, point the policy types' fields at it, then archive the old one by removing its resource.

resources.name: policy_label
resources.description: A label of the credential's Network (the feature `policies`), written by an operator: a free-form tag its policies carry, its name unique in the Network regardless of case. Destroy deletes it and removes it from every policy carrying it.

resources.name: policy_configuration
resources.description: A configuration of the credential's Network (the feature `policies`), written by an operator: values of one of a policy type's configuration types, which policies attach. Its policy type and configuration type never change (a new one replaces it). `body_json` is the body, an object shaped by the configuration type's `fields`, as one `jsonencode()`. Destroy archives it (`ARCHIVED`), refused while a policy that is not archived attaches it: a configuration is archived, never deleted.

destroy.reason: A configuration is archivable (P11): it is never deleted, so destroy archives it (refused while a policy that is not archived attaches it).

resources.name: policy
resources.description: A policy of the credential's Network (the feature `policies`), written by an operator: where (`inventory`) and for which requests (`target`, groups ORed, rows of a group ANDed) a policy type's configurations apply, saved whole in one mutation. Its policy type never changes (a new one replaces it). `inventory` rows are paths by code (`site`, `site/area`, `site/area/slot`, `*` for a whole part, `*` alone for the whole network), written normalized (`SITE`, not `SITE/*`) so the plan stays empty. `labels`, `inventory` and `target` (and each attachment's `target` and `inventory`) are sets, written in any order and replaced whole: each label with both its `id` and its `name`, each target row with its `op` and its `values` (kept in your order, which a match ignores), each value as one `jsonencode()`. `attachments` is a list in your order, each naming a configuration by id (a configuration is its own resource). An attachment's `enabled`, `target` and `inventory` may be left out for their defaults. Destroy archives it (`ARCHIVED`): a policy is archived, never deleted.

actions.name: mobile_config_release
actions.description: Publishes a release of an app's mobile configuration for one environment (the feature `mobile-config`), as a Network admin: compiled, signed and numbered after the last release of the app and environment. A release is immutable, so publishing is an action, not a resource: every invocation is a new release.

ads_enabled.description: Master switch for ad rendering in the app.

actions.name: mobile_config_release_rollback
actions.description: Rolls an app's mobile configuration back to an earlier release (the feature `mobile-config`), as a Network admin: its source is republished as the next release of the app and environment, signed anew.

actions.name: policy_duplicate
actions.description: Duplicates a policy (the feature `policies`), as an operator (D5): a new policy with the same type, context, period, description, labels, target and inventory, attaching the same configurations with their sub-targets and inventory; `<name> (copy)` and `INACTIVE` unless given. Every invocation is a new policy, so it is an action, not a resource: import the copy to manage it.

PolicyStatusFilter.description: Only policies with one of these statuses; repeat the parameter for several (`?status=ACTIVE&status=ARCHIVED`). Left out: every status but `ARCHIVED`.

PolicyContextFilter.name: context
PolicyContextFilter.description: Only policies resolved in this context.

PolicyPathFilter.name: path
PolicyPathFilter.description: Only policies one of whose own inventory includes overlaps this inventory path (`site`, `site/area` or `site/area/slot` by code, `*` for a whole part): on every part both name, one is `*` or they are equal, so `*` matches every policy, `NEWS_APP_IOS` both `NEWS_APP_IOS/home` and `*/home`, `NEWS_APP_IOS/*/right` matches `NEWS_APP_IOS/home` but not `NEWS_APP_IOS/home/top`. Excludes and attachments' rows do not count. A path of the wrong format is 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` at `path`.

ConfigurationSearchFilter.name: q

ConfigurationTypeIdFilter.name: configurationTypeId

PolicyTypeStatusFilter.name: status

IncludeArchived.name: includeArchived
IncludeArchived.description: `true`: the archived ones too, each with its `archivedAt`. `false` or left out: only those not archived.

PlatformFilter.name: platform
PlatformFilter.description: Only those on this platform, a platform key (`APP`, `WEB`).

RequestId.name: X-Request-Id
RequestId.description: Correlation id, 1-128 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`; echoed in the response. A malformed or missing one is replaced by `req_<ULID>`.

XRequestId.description: The request id: the client's well-formed X-Request-Id, else a generated `req_<ULID>`.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when the response is the stored response of an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key.

ValidationFailed.description: The request is not valid (`VALIDATION_FAILED`, `MALFORMED_JSON`, `INVALID_CURSOR`, `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`, `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID`): an unknown query parameter, a malformed value, or a source that does not compile

PolicyConflict.description: Conflict (`IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`; `ALREADY_EXISTS`: a key or position the Network already has; `IN_USE`: a rule of DAS Policies refuses the change while something still uses it, the detail names what; `ARCHIVED`: an archived object takes only the change that restores it; `EDIT_CONFLICT`: the object changed since the `expectedUpdatedAt` the write carries, or a concurrent write or a batch item changed what the write was based on meanwhile. No 409 writes anything; the detail says what happened. A client answers an `EDIT_CONFLICT`, or an `ALREADY_EXISTS`/`IN_USE` a concurrent write caused, by reloading what it changes and reapplying the change)

SigningUnavailable.description: The installation has no signing key for mobile configuration (`NOT_CONFIGURED`), or the Organisation API did not answer for the credential's Network (`UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`)

Forbidden.description: The credential may not do this (`NO_ACCESS`, `INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`, `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE`, `NETWORK_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`, `NETWORK_HOST_MISMATCH`, `FEATURE_DISABLED`)

UpstreamUnavailable.description: The Organisation API did not answer for the credential's Network (`UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`)

InternalError.description: An unexpected failure (`INTERNAL_ERROR`); the request id names it in the service's logs

Money.description: An amount of money: a decimal string (never a JSON number) and its ISO-4217 currency.

siteCode.description: The app the release is for, UPPER_SNAKE, 1-64 characters (e.g. `ONET_IOS`); signed into the bundle as its app id

environment.description: The app's environment the release is for; signed into the bundle in lower case (`production`)

sourceFormat.description: The format of `source`: `DCFG_RULES_V1`, the rules document of segments and flags

source.description: The rules in `sourceFormat`. `DCFG_RULES_V1`: `{ segments?, flags }` - named reusable conditions and the flags by key, each with its `default`, optional `prerequisites` and targeting `rules` (docs/architecture/tag-manager-mobile-config.md "Authoring rules"). Nested at most 100 levels; no key `__proto__`; no U+0000 and no unpaired surrogate in a key or a string

Answered sorted by key

label.description: Name shown in the panel, 1-200 characters; left out, none (the panel shows the key)

fields.description: The schema of the body of its configurations: 0-200 field definitions in the field language of DAS Policies (`{ id, kind, label?, required?, default?, list?, options?, optionsSource?, min?, max?, ... }`; kinds `string`, `int`, `decimal`, `bool`, `section`, `typed`, `map`; `list: true` makes a value a list, of records for a `section`). `optionsSource` names the values a field reads (GET /api/policy-option-sources): a `string` reads a catalogue, `catalogue.<key>`; a `map` reads a mapping, `mapping.<key>`, and holds rows `{ key, cells: [{ to, value? }] }` (e.g. `[{ "key": "320x50", "cells": [{ "to": "GAM" }, { "to": "PREBID" }] }]`). A source the Network has not, or one archived, is 400 `unknown_source`; a `default` is not checked against its catalogue. Stored by the source's id and answered by its key. An invalid definition is 400 at `configurationTypes.<i>.fields.<path>` with the field language's `code`

configurationTypes.description: Its configuration types, 1-50, keys distinct (a type without variants has one, keyed like the type). Answered sorted by key

Audited as `policy-type.update`.

Every rule is checked and every error answered at once (400 at its path with its `code`): `context` one of the type's; at least one inventory include, every inventory path of the right format (`invalid_format`; whether its site, area or slot exists is not checked) and listed once after its normalization; every target row's dimension one of the type's `dimensions` (`dimension_not_assigned`) and its value as the dimension's `input` says; attachments of configurations of the type, not `ARCHIVED` (409 `ARCHIVED` at the attachment), each once, their includes covered by an include of the policy and by none of its excludes (`outside_policy_inventory`); `endAt` after `startAt`. Audited as `policy.create`.

Any subset of its fields; each section sent (`labels`, `inventory`, `target`, `attachments`) replaces that part whole and is checked as on create, and a new inventory is checked against the attachments kept. One mutation, one audit row naming every row changed. Its policy type never changes (400). A policy changed by another write while this one takes its locks is read again once; changed again, 409 `EDIT_CONFLICT` (retry). Attachments keep their ids by configuration.
